theorems.name: Becoming.ScratchCovering.level / step / net / course (definitions)
theorems.in_plain_words: Order L. Let z be the level less what the way takes. The next level is z, plus what the stock gives at z, plus the give of every unit of the way whose need z meets. The way after a step is LineOnAStock.after, unchanged. The net and the course are LineOnAStock's, with this level in place of left.

theorems.name: level_zero
theorems.statement: theorem level_zero (need : U → Nat) (giving : Nat → Nat) (use : U → Nat) (w : List U) (x : Nat) : level need giving use (fun _ => 0) w x = left giving use w x
theorems.in_plain_words: For any need, giving, use, way and level: when no unit puts anything back, the level is LineOnAStock.left. It is stated pointwise because funext would bring in Quot.sound.

theorems.name: course_zero
theorems.statement: theorem course_zero (need : U → Nat) (kids : U → List U) (giving : Nat → Nat) (use : U → Nat) (s : List U × Nat) : ∀ n, course need kids giving use (fun _ => 0) s n = LineOnAStock.course need kids giving use s n
theorems.in_plain_words: For any need, kids, giving, use and start: when no unit puts anything back, the course at every step is LineOnAStock.course.

theorems.name: unending_zero_iff
theorems.statement: theorem unending_zero_iff (need : U → Nat) (kids : U → List U) (giving : Nat → Nat) (use : U → Nat) (s : List U × Nat) : «不穷» (net need kids giving use (fun _ => 0)) «一» s ↔ «不穷» (LineOnAStock.net need kids giving use) «一» s
theorems.in_plain_words: For any need, kids, giving, use and start: when no unit puts anything back, the net never ends exactly where the net of the line on a stock never ends.

theorems.name: ways_alike_any
theorems.statement: theorem ways_alike_any {need : U → Nat} {kids : U → List U} (lv lv' : List U → Nat → Nat) {w : List U} {x x' n : Nat} (alike : ∀ j, j < n → ∀ u, u ∈ (Law.orbit (TurningInTime.pair (after need kids) lv) (w, x) j).1 → (need u ≤ (Law.orbit (TurningInTime.pair (after need kids) lv) (w, x) j).2 ↔ need u ≤ (Law.orbit (TurningInTime.pair (after need kids) lv') (w, x') j).2)) : ∀ j, j ≤ n → (Law.orbit (TurningInTime.pair (after need kids) lv) (w, x) j).1 = (Law.orbit (TurningInTime.pair (after need kids) lv') (w, x') j).1
theorems.in_plain_words: Take any two level laws lv and lv', one need and one kids, one start way w and two start levels x and x'. Suppose that at every step j < n the two levels meet the same needs among the units of the first course's way at j. Then the two ways are equal at every step j ≤ n. Nothing is asked of lv or lv'.

theorems.name: ways_alike_line
theorems.statement: theorem ways_alike_line {need : U → Nat} {kids : U → List U} {g g' : Nat → Nat} {use use' : U → Nat} {w : List U} {x x' n : Nat} (alike : ∀ j, j < n → ∀ u, u ∈ (LineOnAStock.course need kids g use (w, x) j).1 → (need u ≤ (LineOnAStock.course need kids g use (w, x) j).2 ↔ need u ≤ (LineOnAStock.course need kids g' use' (w, x') j).2)) : ∀ j, j ≤ n → (LineOnAStock.course need kids g use (w, x) j).1 = (LineOnAStock.course need kids g' use' (w, x') j).1
theorems.in_plain_words: LineOnAStock.ways_alike, statement verbatim except that course is written LineOnAStock.course. Take two givings, two uses, two start levels, one way, one need and one kids. If at every j < n the two levels meet the same needs of the first course's way, the ways agree at every j ≤ n. It is ways_alike_any at left g use and left g' use', and the proof is one line.

theorems.name: ways_alike_give
theorems.statement: theorem ways_alike_give {need : U → Nat} {kids : U → List U} {g g' : Nat → Nat} {use use' give give' : U → Nat} {w : List U} {x x' n : Nat} (alike : ∀ j, j < n → ∀ u, u ∈ (course need kids g use give (w, x) j).1 → (need u ≤ (course need kids g use give (w, x) j).2 ↔ need u ≤ (course need kids g' use' give' (w, x') j).2)) : ∀ j, j ≤ n → (course need kids g use give (w, x) j).1 = (course need kids g' use' give' (w, x') j).1
theorems.in_plain_words: The same for two courses that also put back, with two givings, two uses, two gives and two start levels. While their levels meet the same needs of the first course's way at every step before n, the ways agree up to n. So what a unit puts back makes no difference to who comes next while the same needs are met. It makes a difference only through the level, at a later step.

theorems.name: step_covered
theorems.statement: theorem step_covered {need use give : U → Nat} {kids : U → List U} {giving : Nat → Nat} (down : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → need v ≤ need u) (covers : ∀ u, taken use (kids u) ≤ give u) {s : List U × Nat} (met : ∀ u, u ∈ s.1 → need u ≤ s.2 - taken use s.1) : (step need kids giving use give s).1 = allKids kids s.1 ∧ s.2 - taken use s.1 ≤ (step need kids giving use give s).2 - taken use (step need kids giving use give s).1 ∧ ∀ v, v ∈ (step need kids giving use give s).1 → need v ≤ (step need kids giving use give s).2 - taken use (step need kids giving use give s).1
theorems.in_plain_words: Premises: kids need no more than their parent; each unit gives at least what its kids together take; any giving; a configuration in which every need of the way is at most what is left. Then after one step the way is all the kids, what is left has not fallen, and every need of the new way is at most what is left after the step.

theorems.name: covered
theorems.statement: theorem covered {need use give : U → Nat} {kids : U → List U} {giving : Nat → Nat} (some : ∀ u, kids u ≠ []) (down : ∀ u v, v ∈ kids u → need v ≤ need u) (covers : ∀ u, taken use (kids u) ≤ give u) {w : List U} {x : Nat} (ne : w ≠ []) (met : ∀ u, u ∈ w → need u ≤ x - taken use w) : (∀ n, (course need kids giving use give (w, x) n).1 = generation kids n w ∧ (∀ u, u ∈ (course need kids giving use give (w, x) n).1 → need u ≤ (course need kids giving use give (w, x) n).2 - taken use (course need kids giving use give (w, x) n).1) ∧ (course need kids giving use give (w, x) n).2 - taken use (course need kids giving use give (w, x) n).1 ≤ (course need kids giving use give (w, x) (n + 1)).2 - taken use (course need kids giving use give (w, x) (n + 1)).1) ∧ «不穷» (net need kids giving use give) «一» (w, x)
theorems.in_plain_words: Premises: every unit has kids; kids need no more than their parent; each unit gives at least what its kids together take; any giving; a way that is not empty, each of whose units needs at most x minus what the way takes. Conclusion: at every step n the way is generation kids n w; every need in it is at most what is left there; what is left at step n + 1 is at least what is left at step n; and the net never ends, stated as «不穷» (net …) «一» (w, x), the form LineOnAStock.unending_iff_holds uses. The way may grow without bound. These are exactly the premises the search proposed, unchanged; I found none extra was needed.

theorems.name: OneKind.only_if
theorems.statement: theorem only_if {a t b k N x : Nat} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (never : «不穷» (net (need a) (kids k) nothing (use t) (give b)) «一» (List.replicate N (), x)) : k * t ≤ b ∧ a + t * N ≤ x
theorems.in_plain_words: One kind of unit: each needs a ≥ 1, takes t, puts back b and leaves k units of the kind. The stock gives nothing of itself. The way starts as N units at level x. If the net never ends, then k*t ≤ b and a + t*N ≤ x. No premise on k or N is used. Why: what is left must meet a at every step, because otherwise nothing is put back and the next level is below a. At step 0 that gives a + t*N ≤ x. If b < k*t, what is left would fall by at least one at every step for ever. So a growing way whose units do not cover what their offspring take comes to an end.

theorems.name: OneKind.unending_iff
theorems.statement: theorem unending_iff {a t b k N x : Nat} (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hN : 1 ≤ N) : «不穷» (net (need a) (kids k) nothing (use t) (give b)) «一» (List.replicate N (), x) ↔ k * t ≤ b ∧ a + t * N ≤ x
theorems.in_plain_words: Same setting, with need a ≥ 1, k ≥ 1 and N ≥ 1. The net never ends if and only if k*t ≤ b and a + t*N ≤ x. The 'if' side is covered and the 'only if' side is only_if.

theorems.name: ScratchMixedWay.course_beside

theorems.in_plain_words: This is (1), the transfer, in LineOnAStock's model as it is, for any need, use, kids and giving, any part c and any start x. theorems.statement: theorem turns_in_time_iff_ends {marked : Nat → Prop} [DecidablePred marked] {alone : W → W} {after : W → Nat → W} {Kept : W → Prop} {giving : Nat → Nat} {use : W → Nat} {H₂ y₂ hi need : Nat} (outside : TurningInTime.AloneOutside marked alone after) (turns : ∀ w x, marked x → Kept (after w x)) (kept : ∀ w x, Kept w → Kept (after w x)) (uses : ∀ w, Kept w → use w = H₂) (nothing : RegimeMargin.FromNothing giving) (short : RegimeMargin.Short giving H₂ y₂) (meets : RegimeMargin.Meets giving H₂ y₂ hi) (keeps : RegimeMargin.Keeps giving H₂ hi) (needs : 0 < need) (within : need ≤ H₂ + y₂) {w : W} {x : Nat} (floor : ∀ j, H₂ ≤ use (Law.orbit alone w j)) (high : x ≤ hi) (ends : ∃ N, (Law.orbit (TurningInTime.asItWas alone (fun w x => RegimeMargin.step giving (use w) x)) (w, x) N).2 < need) : «不穷» (TurningInTime.net need after (fun w x => RegimeMargin.step giving (use w) x)) «一» (w, x) ↔ ∃ T, (∀ j, j < T → need ≤ X j ∧ ¬ marked (X j)) ∧ need ≤ X T ∧ marked (X T) ∧ H₂ + y₂ ≤ X (T + 1)   -- X j written out in the file as (Law.orbit (TurningInTime.asItWas alone (fun w x => RegimeMargin.step giving (use w) x)) (w, x) j).2
theorems.in_plain_words: This is TurningInTime.turns_in_time_iff with short₁, uses₁ and below replaced by two premises. First, every way on alone's orbit from w uses at least H₂ (floor). Second, the course as it was comes to a level below the need at some step (ends). The other premises are the same as there. AloneOutside holds and the marks are decided. A way after a marked step is of the kept kind. Every step keeps that kind, and the kind uses H₂. Nothing is given from nothing. The giving is short of H₂ below y₂ and meets H₂ from y₂ up to hi. The step under H₂ keeps the level within hi. The need is positive and at most H₂ + y₂. The start is at most hi. Conclusion: the line never ends exactly when there is a step T of the course as it was such that: before T the need was met and no level was marked; at T the need is met and the level is marked; at T + 1 the level is at least H₂ + y₂. Lemma asItWas_within shows every level of the course as it was stays at most hi; for that it uses step_more, which says that under a use of at least H₂ the step is the step under H₂ from a lower level.

how_to_tell_it:
The model, named once: the line on a stock (`LineOnAStock`) with one more number per unit, `give`, added to the level after the way's take by each unit whose need is met by what is left (the frozen file's order L).

level_zero, course_zero, unending_zero_iff: When that number is zero for every unit, then for any needs, offspring, stock giving, uses and start, the level after a step, the whole course, and whether the net ever ends are those of the line on a stock as it stands.

ways_alike_any (with ways_alike_line and ways_alike_give as its cases): Take one start way, one need and one offspring rule, two start levels, and any two rules for the next level. If at every step before n the two levels meet the same needs among the units of the first course's way, the two ways are the same at every step up to n. Nothing is asked of the level rules, because the way after a step reads the level only through which needs it meets; so what units add to the level is one more thing that makes no difference to who comes next except through which needs are met. The line's own alikeness law is the case of two levels with nothing added, statement unchanged and proof no shorter.

covered: Suppose every unit of the type has offspring, offspring need no more than their parent, and every unit of the type adds to the level at least what its offspring together take; the stock's own giving may be anything. Start from a way that is not empty, with every unit's need at most what is left of the level after the way's take. Then at every step the way is that generation of the start, every need in it is at most what is left there, what is left is no less than at the step before, and the net never ends. This is sufficient and not necessary, and where offspring take more than their parent it asks each unit to add more than it takes, from nowhere in the model.

OneKind.only_if: One kind of unit that needs a ≥ 1, takes t, adds b and leaves k of its kind, N of them at level x, on a stock that gives nothing of itself: if the net never ends, then k·t ≤ b and a + t·N ≤ x.

OneKind.unending_iff: With also k ≥ 1 and N ≥ 1, the net never ends exactly where k·t ≤ b and a + t·N ≤ x. Each of the three premises a ≥ 1, k ≥ 1, N ≥ 1 is needed, by search and by hand, not in Lean.

Kept.course_values and Kept.side_by_side: One built case. Units that need one, take one and leave two, from one unit at level twelve, on the stock giving min z (12 − z). With nothing added the net ends (the line's own doubling case, carried over by unending_zero_iff). how_to_tell_it:
All of these are in one model, LineOnAStock (units, each with a need, a use and the units it leaves, on a level that after each step is what is left after the units present take, plus what the giving gives on what is left; a unit whose need the level does not meet leaves nothing; the net 'never ends' means some unit's need is met at every step). Below, 'the others' are units each of which leaves only itself, and the way is written as a part c followed by the others R.

course_beside. Suppose every unit of R leaves only itself and R takes H together. Then for any part c, any needs, uses, kids, giving and start: as long as at every earlier step the level of 'c stepping by itself with H added to what it takes' has met the need of every unit of R, the mixed way at this step is that course's way followed by R, at that course's level. Nothing is asked of c.

unending_beside. Suppose R is not empty, every unit of R leaves only itself and needs n, R takes H, and every unit of every generation of c needs at least n. Then, under any giving and use, the net from c followed by R never ends exactly when, on c's own course beside R (H added to its take), the level meets n at every step.

unending_grown. Suppose R is not empty, every unit of R leaves only itself and needs n, R takes H; every unit of c is of a line S; every unit of S needs m; the kids of a unit of S are of S; and n ≤ m. Then, under any giving and use, the net from c followed by R never ends exactly when the level meets n at every step of this course: the part becomes all its kids where the level meets m and nothing where it does not, the level stepping under H plus what the part takes.

turns_in_time_iff_ends (generic, in TurningInTime's terms). It is turns_in_time_iff with three premises exchanged. Kept: outside the marked levels the way after a step is `alone` of the way, and marks are decided; a way after a marked step is of the kept kind; every step keeps that kind; the kind uses H₂; nothing is given from nothing; the giving is short of H₂ below y₂ and meets it from y₂ up to hi; the step under H₂ keeps levels within hi; the need is positive and at most H₂ + y₂; the start is at most hi. In place of short₁, uses₁ and below: every way on `alone`'s orbit uses at least H₂, and the course as it was comes below the need at some step. Conclusion: the line never ends exactly when there is a step T of the course as it was with the need met and no level marked before T, the need met and the level marked at T, and the level at T + 1 at least H₂ + y₂.

mixed_turns_iff. Premises: R is not empty; every unit of R leaves only itself and needs n; R takes H₂; every unit of c is of a line S; every unit of S needs m; the kids of a unit of S are of S; n ≤ m; every unit of S takes at most what its kids take together; nothing is given from nothing; the giving is short of H₂ below y₂ and meets H₂ from y₂ up to hi; the step under H₂ keeps levels within hi; 0 < n ≤ H₂ + y₂; the giving is short of H₂ plus what c takes at every level below y₁; the start x is below H₂ plus what c takes plus y₁, and at most hi. Then the net from c followed by R never ends exactly when there is a step T such that, on the course in which the line's units leave all their kids at every step whatever the level (the level stepping under H₂ plus what they take, from c at x): before T the level is at least m; at T it is below m and still at least n; and at T + 1 it is at least H₂ + y₂. In short: under these premises the growing line is cut off at the first step the level falls below its need, and the rest goes on for ever exactly when n is still met at that step and the level one step later is at or above the level from which the others alone hold. The premises already make the line be cut at some step; the law says what happens to the rest.

mixed_turns_iff_ends. The same conclusion with the same premises, except that 'kids take at least as much', the shortness at H₂ plus c's take, and the start below that point are replaced by one: the course just described (the line leaving all its kids at every step) comes to a level below n at some step. Nothing is asked of what the kids take.

mixed_turns_iff_rising. The same conclusion. Premises: R not empty, each unit of R leaves only itself and needs n, R takes H₂; every unit of c is of S, every unit of S needs m, kids of S are of S, n ≤ m; every unit of S takes strictly less than its kids together; c is not empty; nothing is given from nothing; the giving is short of H₂ below y₂ and meets it from y₂ up to hi; the step with nothing taken keeps every level up to hi within hi; 0 < n ≤ H₂ + y₂; the start is at most hi. Here the ending of the unturned course is derived (its level is nothing at step hi + 1), not given.
